questions.question: Presently Suman is four times as old as her son. Five years ago, she was seven times as old as her son. What is the age of her son?
questions.solution:
Given: Suman is four times as old as her son. Five years ago, she was seven times as old as her son. 

Let the present age or Suman be 'S' and that of her son be 'p'.

According to the question,

S = 4 × p -----------(i)

S - 5 = 7 × (p - 5)

Putting the value of S from equ. (i);

4p - 5 = 7p - 35

7p - 4p = 35 - 5

3p = 30

**p = 10**

Hence, the age of the son of Suman is **10 years.**

• Diwali is observed on Amavasya (or new moon)__ the 15th day of the month of Kartika, every year.

• It is celebrated on the thirteenth lunar day of Krishna Paksha in the Hindu calendar month of Ashvini.

• Parliaments control all the money that governments have. In most countries, and the public money can be spent only when the Parliament sanctions it.

questions.question: The difference between the total revenue and total expenditure of the government is called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**fiscal deficit.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The difference between the total revenue and total expenditure of the government is called a fiscal deficit.**
 
• **A fiscal Deficit:**
 
 
• It is a difference between the total income of the government (total taxes and non-debt capital receipts) and its total expenditure.
 
• A recurring high fiscal deficit means that the government has been spending beyond its means.
 
• The government meets the fiscal deficit by borrowing money. In a way, the total borrowing requirements of the government in a financial year are equal to the fiscal deficit in that year.
 
• A fiscal deficit situation occurs when the government's expenditure exceeds its income.
 
• This difference is calculated both in absolute terms and also as a percentage of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of the country.
 
• **Fiscal Deficit formula:**
 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit = Total expenditure of the government (capital and revenue expenditure) - Total income of the government (Revenue receipts + recovery of loans + other receipts).**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Deflation:**

 
 
• It is a state where** 'Demand is reduced, so definitely its supply get affected and get increased, due to low demand, Price decreases.**
 
• When Price decreases Profit eventually decreases which leads to Unemployment and then affects industries and the closure of companies.
 
 
 
• **The primary Deficit:**
 
 
• It is measured by subtracting the interest payments from the fiscal deficit.
 
• **Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments.**
 
• The primary deficit is a measure of the current year's fiscal operation after excluding the liability of interest payments created due to borrowings of the past.
 
• A primary deficit is considered a tool in the process of bringing more transparency to the government's expenditure pattern.
 
 
 
• **Budget Deficit:**
 
 
• It is the **difference between total expenditure and total receipts.**

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the cost and selling price for a single orange to make the calculation simple and direct.

Cost Price (CP) of 1 orange = 193.20 ÷ 23 = ₹8.40

Selling Price (SP) of 1 orange = 108 ÷ 12 = ₹9.00

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100 = (0.60 ÷ 8.40) × 100

Profit % = (1 ÷ 14) × 100 = 7.14% ≈ 7.1%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

CP of 23 oranges = ₹193.20

SP of 1 dozen (12 oranges) = ₹108

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Selling Price (SP) − Cost Price (CP)

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5608d2799a4f04ef69a8cd20124641f3b7aec78a279ae33eeba93ce1ef2d4cf.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of 1 orange = 193.20 ÷ 23 = ₹8.40

⇒ SP of 1 orange = 108 ÷ 12 = ₹9.00

⇒ Profit earned on 1 orange = 9.00 − 8.40 = ₹0.60

⇒ Profit % = (0.60 ÷ 8.40) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (6 ÷ 84) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 14) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 50 ÷ 7 = 7.1428%

⇒ Correct to one decimal place = 7.1%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The resulting price is Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount.

If a dealer claims to sell goods at Cost Price but uses false weights, Profit % = [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100.
